judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the 'Place a Notice' link in the header's 'Top Links' navigation, with a visually hidden 'Opens in new window'; it goes to https://secure.irishnews.com/notice. On a newspaper's site the link text alone gives its purpose: placing a notice in the paper. I opened the destination: it is the 'Family Notices - IrishNews' page whose heading is 'Create your notice', so the text matches where it leads. No other link in the snapshot has this name (the neighbouring 'Notices' link has a different name and goes to familynotices.irishnews.com), so R1 does not apply. The live page's raw HTML has the same markup as the snapshot, so nothing in the capture differs for this link. The link meets 2.4.4, and Rampa was right to report nothing.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the 'News' link at the top of a list item in the off-canvas Sections Menu flyout; its parent list item also holds the subsections Northern Ireland, Ireland, UK, World and Politics. It goes to /news, which I opened: it redirects to the News section page at /news/. In a site's section menu, 'News' tells users where the link goes. The only other link named 'News' in the snapshot (in the footer) also goes to /news, the same resource, so the shared-name rule (R1) finds nothing to fail. The live raw HTML has the same two identical 'News' links, so nothing in the capture differs. The link meets 2.4.4, and Rampa was right to report nothing.

The link meets 2.4.4, and Rampa was right to report nothing.
